# to pin `&:close({"k":"c"})` with a.k also "c" — the spread shared the
# close call's inner map across applications AND with a move() clone,
# so the last destination's key() resolution was stamped into the
# template and into every child. Applications are now full instances
# canons as written and each child gets ITS OWN key. The move()
# combination moved to the gens row below — its canon mixes the pinned
# move ghost-innard sharing (func.tsv ghost-*) with per-instance
# spread application and no longer reparses without contradiction,
# while its generated output is stable and correct.
# Consecutive bare spreads on SEPARATE LINES (issue #4): the second `&:`
# was read as an operator rather than as a sibling spread. The
# sibling-bare rows above write both spreads on one line; a real document
# writes them down the page, and the newline is exactly what the pair
# close alts had to be taught to see.
# A list spread INSIDE a list spread, with a `key()` in the inner
# template (G8 phase 0). The staging rule is what makes these answer:
# under the pass-count delay it replaced, the inner template was met
# into each element AGAIN on every pass -- ListVal had no
# apply-once-per-element guard, the one MapVal has always had -- so a
# `key()` that had already answered "0" was handed a second, still
# pending copy of itself and the two collided (`scalar_value` at
# $.a.0.k.k). The map-nested row is the control: it went through
